mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is at or below 0.12%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns due to compressed discount rates and increased equity attractiveness relative to fixed income.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative or zero 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.12%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 5.0%, it signals labor market weakness that triggers equity sell-offs due to reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in FEDFUNDS (≤ 0.12%) and rise in UNRATE (> 5.0%) signals a monetary easing cycle coupled with labor market weakness, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days as the Fed's rate cuts support equity valuations.
regime_hint: monetary easing with labor market stress
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.12 and UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (characterized by housing starts above 1200 units), the S&P 500 tends to produce negative 60-day forward returns due to overvaluation and impending economic slowdown as the cycle nears its peak.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances during late-cycle expansion regimes.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) exceed 447,000 million, it signals strong consumer demand that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS exceeds 447,000 million.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105.0, it indicates a contraction in manufacturing and services, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO falls below 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 105.0) and housing starts (HOUST < 1200) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days as recession fears mount.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 105.0 and HOUST < 1200.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle labor market regimes (characterized by payroll employment above 142,000), the S&P 500 tends to produce negative returns over 20 days as the Fed tightens policy to cool the economy and prevent overheating.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances during late-cycle labor market regimes.
